# Atlas operations: synthetic accepted system

This is an isolated contract fixture, not evidence of a real accepted product or rendered dogfood run. Test inputs model a current project-scoped accepted revision `atlas-fixture-1`; real runs must verify actual acceptance provenance and rendered evidence.

## Thesis

A quiet, compact operations workspace whose hierarchy comes from alignment, spacing and text rather than decorative panels.

## Token roles

Use neutral page and raised control surfaces, high-contrast text, muted supporting text, one blue action accent and a distinct semantic warning role. Keep the accepted sans-serif typography voice and spacing scale.

## Component and control grammar

Use labelled controls, visible keyboard focus, inline field validation, compact rows and explicit loading/empty/error/disabled states. A status message has text, an optional icon and an accessible dismiss control; colour is not its only meaning.

## Responsive logic

At narrow widths, navigation collapses to a labelled control. Forms become one column. Primary actions remain reachable without horizontal scrolling. Preserve the existing overview and keyboard path when adding routes.

## Anti-goals

No glass surfaces, decorative gradients, serif typography or replacement of the blue action accent inside this accepted world. These are fixture-wide constraints, not optional page preferences.
